speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; can you describe how it started, such as any recent insect bites, new exposures, or activities you've been doing?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Given your age and sun exposure, does the lesion on your left dorsal hand appear as a solitary, scaly, or pearly bump, or is it more of a diffuse rash with multiple spots? Also, have you noticed any recent changes in its size, color, or if it has begun to bleed or crust over?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. Based on your age, significant sun exposure history, and the description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand without pain or bleeding, this is highly consistent with an actinic keratosis, which is a precancerous lesion caused by UV damage. I recommend a dermatological exam with possible biopsy to confirm and rule out early squamous cell carcinoma.
